_about: Research figures on AI and developer productivity for the Kite Pulse guides. Every figure carries the exact sentence it was taken from and its source page. Read by /blog/measure-developer-productivity-ai (copied into the prototype's RESEARCH on the checked date) and meant for /blog/ai-coding-roi and /blog/ai-coding-data-report. Each study measures something different (a lab task, an enterprise task, experienced developers' own issues), so a figure is quoted with its setting, never alone. Re-check when METR publishes a new uplift study: its February 2026 post says the 2025 result is out of date.
not_used: METR February 2026 point estimates (-18%, CI -38% to +9%; -4%, CI -15% to +9%): the post does not state which way its 'speedup' sign points, so the page quotes METR's own later wording instead (frontier_risk below)
Peng et al. sample size: not in the abstract read
DORA 2024 figures for code quality and review speed: seen only in secondary coverage, not in the primary page read

metr_measured.quote: Surprisingly, we find that allowing AI actually increases completion time by 19%--AI tooling slowed developers down.

metr_forecast_before.quote: Before starting tasks, developers forecast that allowing AI will reduce completion time by 24%.

metr_believed_after.quote: After completing the study, developers estimate that allowing AI reduced completion time by 20%.

metr_experts.quote: This slowdown also contradicts predictions from experts in economics (39% shorter) and ML (38% shorter).

metr_sample.quote: we recruited 16 experienced developers from large open-source repositories
metr_sample.also: Developers provide lists of real issues (246 total)

metr_scope.quote: We do not claim that our developers or repositories represent a majority or plurality of software development work

metr_2026_unreliable.quote: gives us an unreliable signal of the current productivity effect of AI tools

metr_2026_selection.quote: developers choosing not to participate in the study because they do not wish to work without AI

frontier_risk.quote: METR's latest RCT of open source developers using late 2025 public agents found small (~4-20%) productivity benefits, but we expect this to be an underestimate due to selection effects.

peng_faster.quote: The treatment group, with access to the AI pair programmer, completed the task 55.8% faster than the control group.
peng_faster.task: Recruited software developers were asked to implement an HTTP server in JavaScript as quickly as possible.

google_faster.quote: stands at about 21%, although our confidence interval is large
google_faster.sample: Our randomized controlled trial with 96 full-time Google software engineers contributes to this literature
google_faster.caveat: we cannot assume that the effect size obtained in our lab study will necessarily apply more broadly

dora_delivery.quote: As AI adoption increased, it was accompanied by an estimated decrease in delivery throughput by 1.5%, and an estimated reduction in delivery stability by 7.2%.
